```{r setup, include=FALSE}
# All dependencies are explicit; no packages are installed during rendering.
# The analysis needs no Julia rerun and no internet access once sim.Rdata exists.
needed <- c("mgcv", "ggplot2", "patchwork", "knitr", "ggeffects", "ggpubr")
missing_packages <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages)) stop("Install required packages: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "))
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(ggeffects)
library(ggpubr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = TRUE, message = FALSE,
                     fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, out.width = "100%",
                     fig.pos = "H", comment = "#>", dev = "png", dpi = 180)
options(width = 75)
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(params$seed)
out_dir <- params$output_dir
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# How to run this analysis

1. Download the repository using **Code → Download ZIP** and extract it.
2. Open `reintrov_0.4.Rmd` in RStudio. Keep `data/` and `results/` beside it.
3. Install the packages once:

```{r install-instructions, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
install.packages(c("rmarkdown", "knitr", "mgcv", "ggplot2", "patchwork",
                   "ggeffects", "ggpubr"))
```

4. Click **Knit → Knit to HTML**, or run:

```{r run-instructions, eval=FALSE, echo=TRUE}
rmarkdown::render("reintrov_0.4.Rmd")
```

Open `reintrov_0.4.html` to read the figures, marginal-effect plots, model
summaries and diagnostics. Generated outputs are saved in `results/`.
The script reuses the supplied bootstrap checkpoint when its provenance
checks match; a full run computes 200 resamples and can take tens of minutes.

# Analysis overview

The three figures describe community responses to extirpation (four metrics),
predator responses to reintroduction (three metrics), and community responses
to reintroduction (four metrics). Predator biomass and stability are modelled
conditional on establishment. Short/tall trophic-height settings are 2.05/3.43;
high/low predator-survival settings are 1/0.

Reference values (50 resident species, community biomass 100, predator biomass
10, stability 0.1 and evenness 0.1) illustrate changes on a common scale; they
are not measured ecosystem averages or physical units. Inverse-CV stability
0.1 means CV = 10. Confidence intervals describe conditional predictions
within this simulation ensemble, rather than predictions for real releases.

# Input, phases and analysis population

```{r input}
# Load into a private environment to avoid accidental use of unrelated objects.
input_environment <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
load(params$data_file, envir = input_environment)
stopifnot(exists("sim_tom_ok", envir = input_environment, inherits = FALSE))
raw <- as.data.frame(input_environment$sim_tom_ok)
required_columns <- c("sim_id", "Z", "nb_link", "realised_C_1", "realised_S_1",
  "g_1", "delta_g_31", "delta_s_21", "delta_s_32", "delta_sp_32",
  "delta_bmp_31", "delta_stabp_31", "delta_bmc_21", "delta_bmc_32",
  "delta_stabc_21", "delta_stabc_32", "delta_ev_21", "delta_ev_32",
  "stab_com_1", "stab_com_2", "tlvl_mean_1")
stopifnot(all(required_columns %in% names(raw)))

# Apply the two analysis-cohort filters and report both steps.
finite_biomass_ratio <- raw[is.finite(raw$delta_bmp_31), , drop = FALSE]
sims <- finite_biomass_ratio[is.na(finite_biomass_ratio$nb_link), , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(sims$sim_id), nrow(sims) > 0)
cohort <- data.frame(stage = c("Input", "Finite predator biomass ratio",
  "Baseline: no imposed feeding-link change"),
  simulations = c(nrow(raw), nrow(finite_biomass_ratio), nrow(sims)))
knitr::kable(cohort)
write.csv(cohort, file.path(out_dir, "cohort_counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Z remains available in the input; z_1 is the analysis name.
sims$z_1 <- sims$Z
sims$delta_sp_32 <- as.numeric(sims$delta_sp_32)
# These predictors are logged once, before model fitting. Responses are logged in formulas.
stopifnot(all(sims$stab_com_1 > 0), all(sims$stab_com_2 > 0))
sims$stab_com_1 <- log(sims$stab_com_1)
sims$stab_com_2 <- log(sims$stab_com_2)
```

Each row is one simulation trajectory across three phases: intact (1),
extirpated (2) and reintroduced (3). Suffixes `21` and `32` denote ratios
between consecutive phases; `31` compares reintroduced with intact. Evenness
ratios can exceed one, so they are analysed with log-normal linear models,
not beta regression. `data/DATA_DICTIONARY.csv` describes the input columns.

The analysis applies a global finite-predator-biomass-ratio filter.
Before that filter there are `r sum(is.na(raw$nb_link))` baseline records;
`r sum(is.na(raw$nb_link) & !is.finite(raw$delta_bmp_31))` are excluded by it.
Consequently, the binary establishment model is conditional on the retained
analysis cohort, not every attempted simulation. This selection and missing
simulation outputs should be considered when interpreting establishment rates.


# Eleven statistical models

```{r model-specification}
# Keep formulas in one visible registry: this prevents plots and tables from
# silently using different predictor sets. There are no hidden smooth terms
# in the beta GAMs; gam() supplies the beta family and precision estimation.
model_formulas <- list(
  m1 = delta_sp_32 ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 * delta_g_31 + delta_s_21 + z_1,
  m2 = log(delta_stabp_31) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 * delta_g_31 + delta_s_21 + z_1,
  m3 = log(delta_bmp_31) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 * delta_g_31 + delta_s_21 + z_1,
  m4 = delta_s_21 ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 + z_1 + stab_com_1 + tlvl_mean_1,
  m5 = delta_s_32 ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + delta_s_21 + g_1 + z_1 + tlvl_mean_1 + delta_sp_32 + stab_com_2,
  m6 = log(delta_bmc_21) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 + z_1 + stab_com_1 + tlvl_mean_1,
  m7 = log(delta_bmc_32) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + delta_s_21 + g_1 + z_1 + tlvl_mean_1 + delta_sp_32 + stab_com_2,
  m8 = log(delta_stabc_21) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 + z_1 + stab_com_1 + tlvl_mean_1,
  m9 = log(delta_stabc_32) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + delta_s_21 + g_1 + z_1 + tlvl_mean_1 + delta_sp_32 + stab_com_2,
  m10 = log(delta_ev_21) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + g_1 + z_1 + stab_com_1 + tlvl_mean_1,
  m11 = log(delta_ev_32) ~ realised_C_1 * realised_S_1 + delta_s_21 + g_1 + z_1 + tlvl_mean_1 + delta_sp_32 + stab_com_2
)
stopifnot(length(model_formulas) == 11L)
families <- c("binomial logit", rep("Gaussian on log ratio", 2),
  rep("beta logit", 2), rep("Gaussian on log ratio", 6))
model_registry <- data.frame(model = names(model_formulas), family = families,
  formula = vapply(model_formulas, function(f) paste(deparse(f), collapse = " "), character(1)))
knitr::kable(model_registry[c("model", "family")], row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r fit-models}
# Complete and finite cases are selected separately for each model. Explicitly
# evaluating the formula also catches log(0), which complete.cases alone misses.
# For m2/m3, the estimand is the response among established predators.
model_data <- function(id, data) {
  if (id %in% c("m2", "m3")) data <- data[data$delta_sp_32 == 1, , drop = FALSE]
  frame <- suppressWarnings(model.frame(model_formulas[[id]], data = data,
                                       na.action = na.pass))
  valid <- Reduce(`&`, lapply(frame, function(x) if (is.numeric(x)) is.finite(x) else !is.na(x)))
  data[valid, , drop = FALSE]
}
fit_one <- function(id, data) {
  data <- model_data(id, data)
  if (id == "m1") {
    glm(model_formulas[[id]], data = data, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
  } else if (id %in% c("m4", "m5")) {
    mgcv::gam(model_formulas[[id]], data = data, family = mgcv::betar(link = "logit"))
  } else {
    lm(model_formulas[[id]], data = data)
  }
}
models <- setNames(lapply(names(model_formulas), fit_one, data = sims), names(model_formulas))
# Expose the familiar names for users inspecting the knitted workspace.
invisible(list2env(models, envir = environment()))
model_registry$n <- vapply(models, nobs, numeric(1))
model_registry$excluded_from_baseline <- nrow(sims) - model_registry$n
knitr::kable(model_registry[c("model", "family", "n", "excluded_from_baseline")], row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(model_registry, file.path(out_dir, "model_registry.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(models, file.path(out_dir, "models_v0.4.rds"))

# Export unstandardised coefficients with model-specific standard errors.
coefficient_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(id) {
  fit <- models[[id]]
  se <- sqrt(diag(vcov(fit)))
  data.frame(model = id, term = names(coef(fit)), estimate = coef(fit), se = se,
             lower = coef(fit) - qnorm(.975) * se,
             upper = coef(fit) + qnorm(.975) * se, row.names = NULL)
}))
write.csv(coefficient_table, file.path(out_dir, "coefficients.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

`m1` predicts establishment; `m2` and `m3` predict predator stability and
biomass conditional on establishment. Pairs `m4/m5`, `m6/m7`, `m8/m9` and
`m10/m11` describe resident richness, total biomass, community stability and
evenness respectively. These are associations within the simulated ensemble.
In particular, conditioning on predator survival in community models does
not estimate a randomised causal effect of survival.

The richness regressions use `mgcv::betar`,
including its default endpoint adjustment: exact zero/one proportions are
moved just inside the unit interval (`eps = 100 * .Machine$double.eps`).
There are `r sum(sims$delta_s_21 == 1)` exact-one extirpation ratios and
`r sum(sims$delta_s_32 == 1)` exact-one reintroduction ratios. This substantial
boundary mass is a limitation of the beta models; a boundary-aware
alternative would be a separate sensitivity analysis.


# Explicit manuscript scenarios

```{r scenarios}
# A one-factor-at-a-time reference profile reproduces the manuscript design.
# Richness 50 is illustrative (and within the observed 2-59 range), whereas
# all unspecified numeric predictors use their baseline-ensemble means.
reference <- data.frame(realised_C_1 = mean(sims$realised_C_1), realised_S_1 = 50,
  g_1 = mean(sims$g_1), z_1 = mean(sims$z_1), delta_g_31 = mean(sims$delta_g_31),
  delta_s_21 = mean(sims$delta_s_21), delta_sp_32 = mean(sims$delta_sp_32),
  stab_com_1 = mean(sims$stab_com_1), stab_com_2 = mean(sims$stab_com_2),
  tlvl_mean_1 = mean(sims$tlvl_mean_1))
scenario_spec <- data.frame(
  factor = c("Community\nconnectance", "Community\nintactness", "Food-web\ntrophic height",
             "Mass ratio\nPredator:Prey", "Predator\ndiet breadth", "Predator\nsurvival", "Prey\nintactness"),
  variable = c("realised_C_1", "delta_s_21", "tlvl_mean_1", "z_1", "g_1", "delta_sp_32", "delta_g_31"),
  left = c("Strong", "Intact", "Short", "Large", "Large", "High", "Intact"),
  right = c("Weak", "Depleted", "Tall", "Small", "Small", "Low", "Depleted"),
  left_value = c(.09, 1, 2.05, 1000, 12, 1, 1),
  right_value = c(.06, .5, 3.43, 10, 1, 0, .5))
scenarios <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(scenario_spec)), function(i) {
  x <- reference[rep(1, 2), , drop = FALSE]
  x[[scenario_spec$variable[i]]] <- c(scenario_spec$left_value[i], scenario_spec$right_value[i])
  x$factor <- scenario_spec$factor[i]
  x$setting <- c(scenario_spec$left[i], scenario_spec$right[i])
  x$position <- 1:2
  x
}))
scenarios$factor <- factor(scenarios$factor, levels = scenario_spec$factor)
scenario_table <- scenario_spec[c("factor", "left", "left_value", "right", "right_value")]
scenario_table$factor <- gsub("\n", " ", scenario_table$factor)
knitr::kable(scenario_table,
             col.names = c("Factor", "Left", "Value", "Right", "Value"))
write.csv(scenarios, file.path(out_dir, "scenario_predictors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(reference, file.path(out_dir, "reference_predictors.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Predict on the link/log scale, where standard errors are defined. Back-
# transforming gives probabilities or conditional geometric ratios (medians
# under the log-normal model), not bias-corrected arithmetic mean ratios.
predict_link <- function(fit, data) {
  if (inherits(fit, "glm") || inherits(fit, "gam")) {
    p <- predict(fit, newdata = data, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
  } else p <- predict(fit, newdata = data, se.fit = TRUE)
  cbind(estimate = as.numeric(p$fit), se = as.numeric(p$se.fit))
}
ratio_estimate <- function(fit, data) exp(predict_link(fit, data)[, "estimate"])
single_prediction <- function(id, scale = 1) {
  p <- predict_link(models[[id]], scenarios)
  transform <- if (id %in% c("m1", "m4", "m5")) plogis else exp
  data.frame(scenarios[c("factor", "setting", "position")],
    estimate = scale * transform(p[, "estimate"]),
    lower = scale * transform(p[, "estimate"] - qnorm(.975) * p[, "se"]),
    upper = scale * transform(p[, "estimate"] + qnorm(.975) * p[, "se"]))
}
```

These profiles hold unspecified predictors fixed; they do not represent
observed whole communities. Reference log-stability is the mean of logged
stability. Prey intactness, community intactness and survival can therefore
be varied as conditional covariates without simulating a new community.
Some settings are unusual combinations; predictions are not empirical
recommendations about optimal release conditions.
If a scenario variable is absent from a model, changing it leaves that
model's prediction unchanged. For example, the predator-survival setting is
not a predictor in the population models; its identical Figure 2 points
are retained to follow the manuscript's seven-column layout.
Each regression is evaluated separately. A prescribed intactness value in
a second-transition model need not equal the first-transition richness
prediction at the reference profile. Consequently, products of these
predictions are illustrative model comparisons, not reconstructions of a
single internally constrained food-web trajectory.


# Sequential community responses and uncertainty

```{r sequential-bootstrap}
# Figure 3 places both transitions on an intact-community reference scale.
# Products of predicted ratios give the central values. The same resampled
# trajectories refit both stage models, preserving their dependence.
community_ids <- c("m4", "m5", "m6", "m7", "m8", "m9", "m10", "m11")
stage_ratios <- function(fitted) {
  sapply(community_ids, function(id) {
    eta <- predict(fitted[[id]], newdata = scenarios,
                   type = if (inherits(fitted[[id]], "gam")) "link" else "response")
    if (id %in% c("m4", "m5")) plogis(eta) else exp(eta)
  })
}
central_ratios <- stage_ratios(models)
B <- as.integer(params$bootstrap_replicates)
if (!is.finite(B) || B < 100L) stop("Use at least 100 paired bootstrap replicates.")
boot <- array(NA_real_, dim = c(nrow(scenarios), length(community_ids), B),
              dimnames = list(NULL, community_ids, NULL))
bootstrap_errors <- bootstrap_warnings <- character(B)
cache_file <- file.path(out_dir, "paired_bootstrap_predictions.rds")
# A saved bootstrap is reusable only for identical input data, model registry,
# reference/scenario settings, replicate count and seed. This avoids needless
# refitting when rendering the same analysis in HTML.
cache_key <- list(data = unname(tools::md5sum(params$data_file)),
  models = unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(out_dir, "model_registry.csv"))),
  scenarios = unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(out_dir, "scenario_predictors.csv"))),
  B = B, seed = params$seed,
  software = c(R = as.character(getRversion()), mgcv = as.character(packageVersion("mgcv"))))
cached <- if (isTRUE(params$reuse_bootstrap) && file.exists(cache_file)) readRDS(cache_file) else NULL
use_cache <- !is.null(cached) && identical(attr(cached, "cache_key"), cache_key)
if (use_cache) {
  boot <- cached
  bootstrap_errors <- attr(cached, "bootstrap_errors")
  bootstrap_warnings <- attr(cached, "bootstrap_warnings")
  message("Loaded bootstrap/checkpoint with an identical provenance key.")
}
# Checkpoints are saved after each batch of 20. Restarting a matching render
# resumes incomplete replicates. Replicate-specific seeds make results
# independent of worker count and execution order. Windows falls back to one
# worker; on macOS/Linux mclapply uses separate forked R processes.
workers <- max(1L, as.integer(params$bootstrap_workers))
if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") workers <- 1L
bootstrap_one <- function(b) {
  set.seed(params$seed + b)
  sampled <- sims[sample.int(nrow(sims), replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
  warnings <- character()
  error <- ""
  attempt <- tryCatch(withCallingHandlers({
    fitted <- setNames(lapply(community_ids, fit_one, data = sampled), community_ids)
    if (any(!vapply(fitted[c("m4", "m5")], function(x) isTRUE(x$converged), logical(1)))) {
      stop("Beta fit did not converge")
    }
    stage_ratios(fitted)
  }, warning = function(w) {
    warnings <<- c(warnings, conditionMessage(w))
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }), error = function(e) { error <<- conditionMessage(e); NULL })
  list(predictions = attempt, error = error,
       warnings = paste(unique(warnings), collapse = "; "))
}
complete <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) all(is.finite(boot[, , b])), logical(1))
remaining <- which(!complete & bootstrap_errors == "")
if (length(remaining)) for (batch in split(remaining, ceiling(seq_along(remaining) / 20))) {
  batch_results <- parallel::mclapply(batch, bootstrap_one, mc.cores = workers,
                                     mc.preschedule = FALSE, mc.set.seed = FALSE)
  for (j in seq_along(batch)) {
    b <- batch[j]
    result <- batch_results[[j]]
    if (!is.list(result)) stop("A bootstrap worker failed unexpectedly")
    if (!is.null(result$predictions) && all(is.finite(result$predictions))) {
      boot[, , b] <- result$predictions
    } else if (result$error == "") result$error <- "Non-finite bootstrap predictions"
    bootstrap_errors[b] <- result$error
    bootstrap_warnings[b] <- result$warnings
  }
  attr(boot, "cache_key") <- cache_key
  attr(boot, "bootstrap_errors") <- bootstrap_errors
  attr(boot, "bootstrap_warnings") <- bootstrap_warnings
  saveRDS(boot, cache_file)
  writeLines(paste(max(batch), "of", B), file.path(out_dir, "bootstrap_progress.txt"))
  message("Completed bootstrap through ", max(batch), " of ", B)
}
valid_boot <- vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) all(is.finite(boot[, , b])), logical(1))
if (sum(valid_boot) < .9 * B) stop("Too many failed bootstrap fits; inspect bootstrap_errors.")
write.csv(data.frame(replicate = seq_len(B), success = valid_boot,
                     error = bootstrap_errors, warnings = bootstrap_warnings),
          file.path(out_dir, "bootstrap_status.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
attr(boot, "cache_key") <- cache_key
attr(boot, "bootstrap_errors") <- bootstrap_errors
attr(boot, "bootstrap_warnings") <- bootstrap_warnings
saveRDS(boot, cache_file)
boot <- boot[, , valid_boot, drop = FALSE]

community_pairs <- list(Richness = c("m4", "m5"), Biomass = c("m6", "m7"),
                        Stability = c("m8", "m9"), Evenness = c("m10", "m11"))
reference_values <- c(Richness = 50, Biomass = 100, Stability = .1, Evenness = .1)
community_predictions <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(community_pairs), function(metric) {
  ids <- community_pairs[[metric]]
  ref <- reference_values[[metric]]
  stage1 <- boot[, ids[1], ] * ref
  stage2 <- boot[, ids[1], ] * boot[, ids[2], ] * ref
  make_rows <- function(draws, estimate, stage) {
    intervals <- t(apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = c(.025, .975), na.rm = TRUE))
    data.frame(scenarios[c("factor", "setting", "position")], metric = metric, stage = stage,
      estimate = estimate, lower = intervals[, 1], upper = intervals[, 2])
  }
  rbind(make_rows(stage1, ref * central_ratios[, ids[1]], "Post-extirpation"),
        make_rows(stage2, ref * central_ratios[, ids[1]] * central_ratios[, ids[2]], "Post-reintroduction"))
}))
write.csv(community_predictions, file.path(out_dir, "community_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

The paired bootstrap uses `r sum(valid_boot)` successful resamples out of
`r B`, with seed `r params$seed`. It resamples whole simulation records, not
time steps. It assumes the retained simulation records can be treated as
independent sampling units. It does not include uncertainty in the chosen
reference profile or in the underlying food-web parameterisation. More
replicates can be requested through the `bootstrap_replicates` parameter.

`r sum(nzchar(bootstrap_warnings))` resamples generated numerical warnings,
recorded in `bootstrap_status.csv`. In particular, saturated-likelihood
warnings from the inherited beta family must be considered alongside the
large mass at persistence = 1; convergence alone does not establish that
this distributional specification is appropriate.

```{r bootstrap-warning-summary}
warning_counts <- table(bootstrap_warnings[nzchar(bootstrap_warnings)])
if (length(warning_counts)) knitr::kable(data.frame(
  warning = names(warning_counts), replicates = as.integer(warning_counts)))
```


# Results figures

```{r figure-functions}
# A shared plotting function makes row order, colours, symbols and labels
# consistent across all three figures. Error bars are never clipped by hard
# y-limits; scale differences are allowed where the new results require them.
scenario_colours <- setNames(c("#1c355e", "#719891", "#c9b3ab", "#9e1420",
                               "#ef7800", "#6fa5bc", "#ab746d"), scenario_spec$factor)
plot_row <- function(data, metric, ref, letter, comparison = FALSE, top = FALSE,
                     probability = FALSE, population = FALSE) {
  data$factor <- droplevels(data$factor)
  data$alpha <- if (comparison) ifelse(data$stage == "Post-extirpation", .35, 1) else 1
  data$shape <- if (comparison) ifelse(data$stage == "Post-extirpation", 16, 15) else 16
  data$x <- data$position + if (comparison) ifelse(data$stage == "Post-extirpation", -.07, .07) else 0
  panel <- ggplot(data, aes(x = x, y = estimate, colour = factor)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ref, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = .35, colour = "grey25") +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, alpha = alpha), linewidth = .35) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = shape, alpha = alpha), size = 2.4) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = scenario_colours, guide = "none") +
    scale_alpha_identity() + scale_shape_identity() +
    facet_grid(. ~ factor) +
    # Scenario-specific labels share numeric positions, so use a separate
    # text layer instead of forcing identical x labels in every facet.
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1, 2), labels = c("", ""), limits = c(.55, 2.45)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) +
    theme(strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = if (top) element_text(size = 8) else element_blank(),
          axis.line.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_blank(), panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(.14, "in"),
          plot.margin = margin(2, 4, 15, 2))
  labels <- unique(data[c("factor", "setting", "position")])
  labels$label_y <- if (metric == "Stability")
    10^floor(min(log10(c(data$lower, data$upper, ref))) - .05) else -Inf
  panel <- panel + geom_text(data = labels,
    aes(x = position, y = label_y, label = setting), inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = 1.5, size = 2.8) + coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
  baseline <- ggplot(data.frame(x = 1, y = ref), aes(x, y)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ref, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = .35, colour = "grey25") +
    geom_point(size = 2.4, colour = "grey30") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1,
      labels = if (population) "Average\npredator" else "Average\ncommunity",
      limits = c(.55, 1.45)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = metric, tag = letter) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 10) + theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold"),
      plot.margin = margin(2, 4, 15, 4), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8))
  yrange <- range(c(data$lower, data$upper, ref), finite = TRUE)
  if (metric == "Stability") {
    # Positive log-scale limits include all data and the illustrative baseline.
    logrange <- c(floor(min(log10(yrange)) - .05), ceiling(max(log10(yrange)) + .05))
    log_breaks <- 10^seq(logrange[1], logrange[2])
    log_labels <- function(x) parse(text = paste0("10^", round(log10(x))))
    panel <- panel + scale_y_log10(limits = 10^logrange, breaks = log_breaks,
      labels = log_labels, expand = expansion(mult = 0))
    baseline <- baseline + scale_y_log10(limits = 10^logrange, breaks = log_breaks,
      labels = log_labels, expand = expansion(mult = 0))
  } else {
    pad <- max(diff(yrange) * .15, abs(ref) * .04)
    limits <- yrange + c(-pad, pad)
    if (probability) limits <- c(max(0, limits[1]), min(1.01, limits[2]))
    panel <- panel + scale_y_continuous(limits = limits)
    baseline <- baseline + scale_y_continuous(limits = limits)
  }
  baseline + panel + plot_layout(widths = c(1.1, 2 * nlevels(data$factor)))
}
save_figure <- function(plot, stem, height) {
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(stem, ".pdf")), plot, width = 12, height = height,
         device = grDevices::cairo_pdf)
  ggsave(file.path(out_dir, paste0(stem, ".png")), plot, width = 12, height = height,
         dpi = 300, bg = "white")
}
```

## Figure 1: community responses to extirpation

```{r figure-1, fig.height=8, fig.cap="Conditional community responses to predator extirpation. Four metrics and four scenario pairs follow the manuscript layout. Dots are model predictions; intervals are 95% paired-bootstrap intervals. Dashed lines show illustrative intact reference values. Stability uses a logarithmic axis."}
extirpation_factors <- scenario_spec$factor[c(1, 3, 4, 5)]
fig1_data <- subset(community_predictions,
                    stage == "Post-extirpation" & factor %in% extirpation_factors)
fig1_data$factor <- factor(fig1_data$factor, levels = extirpation_factors)
fig1 <- wrap_plots(lapply(seq_along(community_pairs), function(i) {
  metric <- names(community_pairs)[i]
  plot_row(subset(fig1_data, metric == names(community_pairs)[i]), metric,
           reference_values[[metric]], LETTERS[i], top = i == 1)
}), ncol = 1) + plot_annotation(title = "Intact                                     Post-extirpation")
save_figure(fig1, "figure_1_extirpation", 8)
fig1
```


## Figure 2: predator responses to reintroduction

```{r figure-2, fig.height=7, fig.cap="Predator establishment probability, biomass and temporal stability. Biomass and stability predictions are conditional on predator establishment. Intervals are pointwise 95% model confidence intervals, transformed from the link/log scale. The population reference values are probability 1, biomass 10 and inverse-CV stability 0.1."}
population_predictions <- rbind(
  transform(single_prediction("m1"), metric = "Establishment"),
  transform(single_prediction("m3", 10), metric = "Biomass"),
  transform(single_prediction("m2", .1), metric = "Stability"))
write.csv(population_predictions, file.path(out_dir, "predator_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
population_metrics <- c("Establishment", "Biomass", "Stability")
population_reference <- c(Establishment = 1, Biomass = 10, Stability = .1)
fig2 <- wrap_plots(lapply(seq_along(population_metrics), function(i) {
  metric <- population_metrics[i]
  plot_row(subset(population_predictions, metric == population_metrics[i]), metric,
           population_reference[[metric]], LETTERS[i], top = i == 1,
           probability = metric == "Establishment", population = TRUE)
}), ncol = 1) + plot_annotation(title = "Intact                                     Post-reintroduction")
save_figure(fig2, "figure_2_predator", 7)
fig2
```


## Figure 3: community responses after reintroduction

```{r figure-3, fig.height=9, fig.cap="Community responses on a common intact-reference scale. Transparent circles show post-extirpation predictions and opaque squares show post-reintroduction predictions. Reintroduction values combine both sequential model ratios. Intervals propagate their dependence using the paired bootstrap. "}
fig3 <- wrap_plots(lapply(seq_along(community_pairs), function(i) {
  metric <- names(community_pairs)[i]
  plot_row(subset(community_predictions, metric == names(community_pairs)[i]), metric,
           reference_values[[metric]], LETTERS[i], comparison = TRUE, top = i == 1)
}), ncol = 1) + plot_annotation(title = "Intact                                     Post-extirpation / post-reintroduction")
save_figure(fig3, "figure_3_reintroduction", 9)
fig3
```


# Marginal-effect plots

These panels show the fitted response across each predictor and the modelled
interactions, with pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Unspecified predictors
are held at their model-data means. Continuous response models display log
ratios; establishment and richness models display probabilities or proportions.
Prediction grids show the ranges specified in the plotting code and can extend
beyond the observed data. Interpret extrapolated portions accordingly.

```{r marginal-plot-style, include=FALSE}
# Shared colours for the richness and predator-diet interaction curves.
palette_3 <- c("#604087", "#4f67a1", "#659c75")
```

  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Probability population reestabilshes", y = "\u0394 Community evenness") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic()

m11_g = ggpredict(m11, "g_1 [0:20, by = 0.1]", back_transform = F)
plt_m11_g = ggplot(m11_g) +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = predicted)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), alpha = 0.1) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Predator diet breadth", y = "\u0394 Community evenness") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic()

m11_c_s = ggpredict(m11, terms = c("realised_C_1 [0:0.3, by = 0.01]", "realised_S_1 [5, 15, 50]"), back_transform = F)
plt_m11_c_s = ggplot(m11_c_s) +
  geom_line(aes(x = x, y = predicted, colour = group)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(x = x, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high, fill = group), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = 0), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Connectance", y = "\u0394 Community evenness") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette_3, name = "Richness") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette_3, name = "Richness") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


ggarrange(
  ggarrange(plt_m11_z, plt_m11_tlvl, plt_m11_g, plt_m11_deltas_21, plt_m11_cv_com, plt_m11_deltasp_32, ncol = 2, nrow = 3, align = "h", labels = c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"), heights = c(1)),
  plt_m11_c_s, 
  ncol = 2, nrow = 1, widths = c(1,0.7), labels = c("", "G"))

```

# Model diagnostics and detailed results

```{r diagnostics}
# Diagnostics are descriptive checks, not a claim that the log-normal or beta
# distributions are true. Examine residual shape, heteroscedasticity and high
# leverage before using these results in a final manuscript.
diagnostics <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(id) {
  fit <- models[[id]]
  r <- residuals(fit, type = "pearson")
  data.frame(model = id, n = nobs(fit), AIC = AIC(fit),
    residual_sd = sd(r), maximum_absolute_residual = max(abs(r)),
    converged = if (inherits(fit, "gam") || inherits(fit, "glm")) isTRUE(fit$converged) else TRUE)
}))
knitr::kable(diagnostics, digits = 4,
             col.names = c("Model", "n", "AIC", "Residual SD", "Max residual", "Converged"))
stopifnot(all(diagnostics$converged), all(is.finite(coefficient_table$estimate)),
          all(is.finite(coefficient_table$se)),
          all(community_predictions$lower <= community_predictions$upper),
          all(population_predictions$lower <= population_predictions$upper))
write.csv(diagnostics, file.path(out_dir, "model_diagnostics.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r residual-plots, fig.height=8}
diagnostic_points <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(models), function(id) {
  data.frame(model = id, fitted = fitted(models[[id]]),
             residual = residuals(models[[id]], type = "pearson"))
}))
ggplot(diagnostic_points, aes(fitted, residual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .08, size = .3) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~ factor(model, levels = names(models)), scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) + labs(x = "Fitted value", y = "Pearson residual")
```

```{r detailed-model-summaries, results='asis'}
# Complete summaries retain coefficients, residual summaries and family details.
# Printing one model per subsection makes every fitted model auditable.
for (id in names(models)) {
  cat("\n\n## ", id, "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("Formula:\n\n```\n",
      paste(strwrap(model_registry$formula[model_registry$model == id], width = 72),
            collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n\n")
  cat("```\n", paste(capture.output(summary(models[[id]])), collapse = "\n"), "\n```\n")
}
```

# Reproducibility and interpretation

All eleven models are fitted from the supplied input. The simulation data are
unchanged; this script performs statistical analysis rather than rerunning the
Julia simulations. The precise source revision that generated every historical
simulation output has not been established.

Predictions vary one scenario at a time while other predictors stay at the
reference profile displayed above. They describe conditional associations;
prey-species persistence is distinct from prey biomass or production. These
models do not establish a causal benefit of prey loss. Exponentiated log-model
predictions are geometric ratios, rather than arithmetic means.

The results folder contains model sample sizes, coefficients, predictor
profiles, predictions, diagnostics, bootstrap status, fitted models and
standalone figure files. Model warnings and boundary-proportion limitations
are reported explicitly. Package versions for this execution follow.
